sentenceSets.sentence: She kept the confidence inviolate, even when telling it would have materially helped her own position.

answerChoices.reasoning: Secret describes the information's status, but the sentence is about her conduct under temptation—what she refused to do when disclosure would have paid.
Intact would say nothing had been damaged, while the pressure the sentence describes is specifically to speak.
Sacrosanct means everyone regards the thing as untouchable, whereas the sentence shows her alone deciding to honor it against her own interest.
Confidential describes how the information was classified when it was given to her, not whether she honored that classification when it cost her.
Private describes the kind of matter involved, and the sentence is about what she did with it rather than what sort of thing it was.
Sealed suggests a physical document closed against inspection, but the confidence here is something she could simply have said aloud.
Hidden implies active concealment from searchers, while the sentence describes her declining an opportunity to speak.
Guarded describes wariness in how one speaks, which falls short of the flat refusal the sentence records even at a cost to herself.
Making it public is exactly what she declined to do.
Compromised would mean the confidence had been broken, contradicting the sentence.
Notorious means widely and unfavorably known, the opposite of something she kept to herself.

sentenceSets.sentence: The treaty promised that the burial grounds would remain inviolate, a promise the survey crews broke within eleven years.

answerChoices.reasoning: Undisturbed describes a physical condition that weather or animals could upset just as easily, while the sentence names human crews breaking a promise, which makes the guarantee one against entry by right.
Protected implies someone posted to guard the site, but the treaty's promise was that no one would come, not that anyone would stand watch.
Sacred concerns the site's religious standing, which a treaty can acknowledge but cannot confer or withdraw.
Untouched reports a state of affairs, whereas what the crews violated was an undertaking that the ground was not to be entered at all.
Unmarked would mean no boundary or monument was set up, but a treaty securing burial grounds would more likely mark them than hide them.
Preserved implies active upkeep, which is a different obligation from leaving a place alone.
Fenced describes a physical barrier, and the sentence's promise is a legal undertaking that crews later disregarded.
Restricted implies access granted under conditions, while the promise the crews broke admitted of no conditions.
Excavation is what breaking the promise would amount to, not what the treaty guaranteed.
Development of the ground is the opposite of what a treaty protecting burial grounds would promise.
Forfeited would mean the ground was surrendered, which no one would promise on behalf of a burial site.

sentenceSets.sentence: He treated the rule against speaking to reporters as inviolate, and twenty years of pressure never produced an exception.

answerChoices.reasoning: Absolute describes the wording of a rule as admitting no degrees, but the evidence the sentence offers is about his own conduct over twenty years, not about how the rule was drafted.
Binding means formally enforceable by someone else, while the sentence shows him honoring the rule by his own resolve under pressure.
Unconditional describes a rule written without provisos, whereas what the sentence records is that no circumstance ever moved him to set it aside.
Rigid is ordinarily a complaint about inflexibility, yet the sentence presents twenty years without an exception as a record he kept rather than a fault.
Permanent concerns how long the rule stays in force, not whether he would break it when pressed.
Immutable means the rule cannot be amended, but the sentence is about his obedience to it rather than anyone's power to rewrite it.
Explicit describes clarity of wording, which would not by itself explain twenty years of unbroken compliance.
Customary would make the rule a habit others share, while the sentence singles out how he in particular treated it.
Negotiable would invite exactly the exceptions the sentence says were never made.
Optional would mean the rule could be ignored at will, contradicting twenty years of pressure failing to move him.
Obsolete would mean the rule no longer applied, leaving nothing for the pressure to test.
